R7BL-bear-drive-0001.name: 5.1 km W of Shekilie River
R7BL-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7BL-bear-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2012 (14 years old), 290 m S: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire G92498), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Unnamed wetland 80 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 236 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Sierra Yoyo Desan Rd, Kotcho Mainline.
Park: 58.9544, -120.32712, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 290 m E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 0 m, about 6 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-56, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2020-02-25, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BL-bear-drive-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-56: about 94 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.3 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
4 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
2 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).
